chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Majilawayh ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharija, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

If one of you desires a matter, let him not consult anyone among the people regarding it until he consults Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. I said: And what is consulting Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He? He said: He begins by invoking Allah for guidance in it first, and then he consults regarding it. If he begins with Allah, Exalted and Glorious, then Allah will cause goodness to flow for him through the tongue of whom He wills among the creation.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of consulting Allah and people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to clarify the sequence of consultation, establishing that *istikhara* (seeking divine preference) must precede human advice to ensure the decision is rooted in spiritual alignment. This methodology reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating divine will with practical wisdom, where prioritizing Allah’s guidance ensures that the subsequent human counsel serves as a vehicle for the chosen outcome.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasim Majilawayh, from Muhammed bin Ali al-Kufi, from Uthman bin Isa, from Harun bin Kharija, that he said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:

If one of you wants a thing, let him, verily, not consult anyone of the people about it until he consults Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He. I said: And what is consulting Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He? So he said: That he begins by invoking Allah for guidance in it at first, and then he would consult about it. If he begins with Allah, then Allah, Exalted and Glorious, will make good flow to him on the tongue of whom He likes among the creation.
